title: Küçüksu Pavilion & Anadolu Hisarı: Asian-Shore Ottoman Hunting Lodge
metaDescription: Visit Küçüksu Pavilion beneath the FSM Bridge: 2026 Milli Saraylar hours, Monday closures, Göksu River cafes, Beylerbeyi pairing, and yacht drop-offs.
quickAnswer: Küçüksu Pavilion is a compact 1856–1857 Ottoman imperial hunting lodge on Istanbul's Asian Bosphorus shore, directly beneath the Fatih Sultan Mehmet Bridge. Open Tuesday through Sunday (09:00–17:00 ticket office), it costs 300 TL for foreign visitors in 2026 and pairs naturally with Anadolu Hisarı, Göksu River cafes, and Beylerbeyi Palace.
category: Inner Pages — 20 Deep Istanbul Practical & Hidden-Gem Guides

body.text: How do you visit Küçüksu Pavilion right beneath the Fatih Sultan Mehmet Bridge?

Reach Küçüksu Pavilion (Göksu Mah., Küçüksu Cad. No:12, Beykoz) by taking a public [Şehir Hatları ferry](https://sehirhatlari.istanbul/en/timetables) to Küçüksu or Anadolu Hisarı Pier, or by taxi/private car along the Asian coastal road from Üsküdar in 20–30 minutes. Foreign-visitor interior admission is 300 TL in 2026 ([Milli Saraylar](https://www.millisaraylar.gov.tr/Lokasyon/6/Kucuksu-Kasri)).

Commissioned by Sultan Abdülmecid in 1856–1857 to replace an earlier 1751 wooden kiosk, the three-story masonry lodge served as a daytime retreat ("biniş kasrı") rather than an overnight palace—there are no bedrooms. Inside, four corner rooms open onto central halls on each main floor, showcasing Italian marble fireplaces, marquetry parquet floors, and European-style stucco ceilings ([Milli Saraylar](https://www.millisaraylar.gov.tr/Lokasyon/6/Kucuksu-Kasri)). Allow 35 to 45 minutes for the guided interior walk, plus time on the waterfront lawn directly facing Rumeli Fortress across the narrowest channel of the Bosphorus. The separate Küçüksu Picnic Area (Mesire Alanı) carries a 500 TL foreign-visitor entry fee and is free for children under 12.

Küçüksu Pavilion is closed every Monday, along with New Year's Day and the first day of both Ramadan Bayram (Eid al-Fitr) and Kurban Bayram (Eid al-Adha). On Tuesday through Sunday, the ticket office operates from 09:00 to 17:00 and grounds stay open until 17:30 ([Milli Saraylar](https://www.millisaraylar.gov.tr/Lokasyon/6/Kucuksu-Kasri)).

Because [Beylerbeyi Palace](https://www.millisaraylar.gov.tr/Lokasyon/4/Beylerbeyi-Sarayi) and Dolmabahçe Palace also close on Mondays, scheduling an Asian-shore palace loop on a Monday means finding locked gates at both estates. If a public holiday falls on a Monday, the pavilion remains closed. Aim for a Tuesday–Thursday morning arrival at 09:30 to walk the rooms without tour-bus queues and catch crisp morning light on the carved sea facade.
How do you combine it with Göksu River cafes and Beylerbeyi?

Start at Beylerbeyi Palace at 09:00, drive 15 minutes north along the Bosphorus shore to Küçüksu Pavilion by 11:00, walk five minutes north to 14th-century Anadolu Hisarı, and finish with a late lunch along the Göksu Stream. Reversing the order works equally well if you arrive by ferry from Bebek or Emirgan.
Here is a clean half-day checklist for the Asian Bosphorus shore:

items: Verify Monday closures: Confirm your day of week before booking a driver or boat, as both National Palaces sites close Mondays.
Start early at Beylerbeyi: Foreign-visitor tickets are 800 TL in 2026 ([Istanbul.com](https://istanbul.com/beylerbeyi-palace)); photography is restricted inside the main halls.
Walk the Göksu Creek footbridge: Small wooden boats moor right beside outdoor breakfast and fish terraces along the creek.

Check ferry return times: [Şehir Hatları](https://sehirhatlari.istanbul/en/price-list) commuter boats link Anadolu Hisarı and Küçüksu to European-side piers like Bebek, Emirgan, and Beşiktaş at set intervals.

Pack a wind layer: Even in spring and autumn, the channel beneath the Fatih Sultan Mehmet Bridge funnels a brisk breeze—see our [Türkiye winter travel guide](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/blog/turkey-in-winter-premium-travel-guide) for seasonal packing notes.

body.text: Can a private Bosphorus yacht drop you near the pavilion?

Yes, private Bosphorus yachts can drop off and pick up passengers at the public Küçüksu Pier (Küçüksu İskelesi) or nearby Anadolu Hisarı Pier, just a two-minute walk from the pavilion gate. Yachts cannot tie up directly at the museum's historic marble sea stairs, so captains use the adjacent municipal dock for brief embarkation.

Plan a 10-minute loading window: the Bosphorus current runs swiftly past the narrow strait here, and commuter ferries always have docking priority at Küçüksu Pier. Coordinate your exact pickup time with the captain via phone or WhatsApp while you finish tea along the Göksu Stream. faq.q: Is the MuseumPass Istanbul valid at Küçüksu Pavilion?
faq.a: No. Küçüksu Pavilion is managed by the Directorate of National Palaces (Milli Saraylar), not the Ministry of Culture, so foreign visitors buy a separate 300 TL ticket or a National Palaces Pass at the gate.

faq.q: How long do you need to visit Küçüksu Pavilion?
faq.a: Plan 35 to 45 minutes for the two main interior floors and another 20 minutes for the waterfront garden and tea terrace overlooking the Bosphorus.

faq.q: Can you take photos inside Küçüksu Pavilion?
faq.a: No interior photography or video is permitted inside the furnished palace rooms, though you may photograph the ornate exterior facade, fountain, and Bosphorus shoreline freely.

faq.q: Is Küçüksu Pavilion open on Turkish national holidays?
faq.a: Yes, on most secular national holidays such as April 23, May 19, August 30, and October 29 (unless they fall on a Monday). It is closed on January 1 and the first day of Ramadan and Kurban Bayram.

faq.q: How do you cross from Bebek or Rumeli Hisarı to Küçüksu?
faq.a: Take the short Şehir Hatları Bosphorus ferry connecting Emirgan/Aşiyan/Bebek to Küçüksu or Anadolu Hisarı Pier, which crosses the strait in roughly 10 to 15 minutes.

faq.q: Are there luggage lockers at Küçüksu Pavilion?
faq.a: Small handbags are allowed after security screening, but there is no large-suitcase storage on site; leave heavy luggage at your hotel or in your private vehicle.
